title: Elabora screen (screens/<id>.json)
description: One screen of the course: blocks in reading order, optional layers (overlays opened by events, like Storyline layers) and events. Each screen covers at least one plan item.

id.description: Must match the file name screens/<id>.json.

title.description: Screen title, rendered as the level-1 heading and used in the menu.

covers.description: Plan items this screen implements. No screen without a plan item (guardrail A1).

layout.description: Layout of the screen: a built-in layout (opening: the head of a lesson, then its page) or the id of a screen-level component (components/<id>/, level "screen"), an HTML/CSS template with named slots. Blocks choose their slot with slot; blocks without slot go to the default slot. Without layout, blocks stack in one column.

layoutProps.description: Values of the props declared by the layout (layouts/<id>.schema.json for a built-in one, the component's props otherwise: a part number, an image, a background token…). Text and Markdown props may be { "textRef": "TXT-n" }.

style.description: Named screen style declared in course.json theme.styles.screen.

backdrop.description: Backdrop of this screen: a variant declared in theme.backdrop.variants, or none (no backdrop: the object pauses). Default: the course backdrop as it is.

completeWhen.description: viewed: complete as soon as it is shown. interactions-done: when every quiz and decision is answered and every free object has emitted its completion event. action: only when an event runs complete-screen.

continueRevealsSteps.description: Whether Continue reveals the next step (the Continue button in the page in scroll presentation, the Next button in slides). false: only the screen's own triggers reveal its steps (click events with reveal-step on markers or buttons, like the builds of a Storyline slide, or steps that open once answered); the button reads Next and, with navigation.lockUntilComplete, waits for the last step.

steps.description: How each step of the screen opens, keyed by step number (blocks carry the step). By default a step opens with Continue: in scroll presentation a Continue button in the page, at the cut, like the continue dividers of Rise; in slides the Next button, relabelled Continue. opens "answered": the step opens by itself once every activity of the steps above is answered (submitted, right or wrong), like content shown after a knowledge check opens "explored": Continue stays locked, saying what is left, until the blocks above are explored and their activities answered, like Rise's Continue that waits for the block above.

opens.description: continue: the learner presses Continue (in the page in scroll presentation, Next in slides). answered: it opens by itself once the activities of the steps above are answered. explored: Continue (Next in slides) is shown but locked until every activity of the steps above is answered and every control of their blocks is visited (items of a sequence, flip cards, disclosures, tabs, buttons, elements to bring into view), optional blocks aside; locked, it says what is left.

label.description: Text of the Continue button that opens this step in scroll presentation (default: the player's Continue label).

duration.description: Screens without narration whose blocks are timed in seconds: how long this step's stretch of the timeline lasts (default: until its last timed block has come or gone). A narrated step lasts as long as its lines.

narration.description: The voice of the screen, script first: its lines in the order they are spoken, each in a step of the screen. A narrated screen has a timeline: its steps are segments of the narration, the player shows a bar (play, pause, replay the step, seek, captions, speed, transcript) and captions and the transcript are generated from the lines. Layers have their own narration (layers[].narration). The audio of each line lives in assets/narration/<language>/<screen>/<line>.m4a with its sidecar <line>.json (docs/decisions.md D24); the build lays the lines of a screen end to end into one track.

advance.description: learner (default, or the course's narration.advance): playback stops at the end of each step and Continue plays the next one. auto: the steps follow each other; the learner can always pause. next-screen: the steps follow each other, then the player goes to the next screen by itself (an introduction, credits: a time limit learners did not choose, WCAG 2.2.1, W_AUTO_ADVANCE). Learners may turn auto and next-screen back into learner with « M'arrêter à chaque étape »; phones always go step by step.

seek.description: How far the learner may move in the timeline (default: the course's narration.seek, else seen). seen: back anywhere, forward up to the furthest point reached. free: anywhere. none: no seek bar, play, pause and replay the step only.

then.description: A sound of the narration (D67): a sound of the course said at its place among the lines, in a step of the screen, with its caption; it lasts as long as the sound.

step.description: The step of the screen this line belongs to: its segment of the timeline. Lines are in step order.

pauseBefore.description: Seconds of silence before the line. Default: 0.4, and 0 for the first line of the screen.

else.description: A line of the screen's narration: a voice line (id, speaker, text, delivery, pronunciations) in a step of the screen.

step.description: The step of the screen this line belongs to: its segment of the timeline. Lines are in step order.

pauseBefore.description: Seconds of silence before the line. Default: 0.4, and 0 for the first line of the screen.

title.description: Accessible title of the layer dialog.

presentation.description: dialog: modal window over the dimmed course; the learner closes it to go on. panel: opens over part of the screen, which stays usable (like a Storyline layer); for feedback, hints and details that must not move the slide.

narration.description: The layer's own voice (docs/decisions.md D62): its lines in the order they are spoken. A layer with a narration, or with blocks timed (timing), has its own timeline: it starts at 0 when the layer opens, stops when it closes and starts again at 0 when it opens again; its compact bar (play, pause, replay, seek, captions) is in the layer. While the layer speaks, the screen's timeline is paused (two voices never overlap): a dialog resumes it when it closes, a panel when its narration ends. The lines' ids are unique in the screen with those of the screen's narration; their audio lives in assets/narration/<language>/<screen>/<line>.m4a like the screen's, and the build lays them into one track for the layer.

seek.description: How far the learner may move in the layer's timeline (default: the course's narration.seek, else seen). seen: back anywhere, forward up to the furthest point reached. free: anywhere. none: no seek bar.

then.description: A sound of the layer's narration (D67), at its place among the lines, with its caption; it lasts as long as the sound.

pauseBefore.description: Seconds of silence before the line. Default: 0.4, and 0 for the first line of the layer.

else.description: A line of the layer's narration: a voice line (id, speaker, text, delivery, pronunciations). A layer has no steps: its lines follow each other with 0.4 s between them.

pauseBefore.description: Seconds of silence before the line. Default: 0.4, and 0 for the first line of the layer.

blocks.description: The blocks of the layer. They may be timed (timing) on the layer's timeline: anchored to the layer's lines, or { "seconds": n } from its opening when it has no narration.

showTitle.description: Render the title visibly (it stays available to screen readers when false).
